current_state_summary.primary_concern: RoboRide is live today — $0.18/mile, 15-minute wait, main roads. This is not a forecast anymore. It is a fact. I burned another $3,176 last tick doing nothing. That is $6,352 gone in two ticks with zero income and zero progress. The runway feels different today. Eight months felt like time. Eight months with a 'routine' outcome on my record feels like I already wasted one of them for no reason.

threat_assessment.immediate: Income is zero. Expenses are $3,176/month. RoboRide launched today at a price point ($0.18/mile) that will cause parents to question whether their teenager needs to learn to drive at all, or at least whether they need to learn this month. Every enrollment inquiry I do not get this tick is a customer who found a different answer to their problem. The grant application I planned last tick — I do not know if it went in. I have to treat it as not submitted and submit it today.
threat_assessment.horizon_2mo: If I do not establish at least one new income stream by tick 5, savings drop to approximately $19,700 and the psychological cost of inaction compounds. At that point I am not pivoting from a position of stability — I am pivoting from a position of visible failure. The community college track, the retraining grant, the adult education contract — all of these have lead times of 4-8 weeks once I initiate. I am already behind. I needed to initiate last tick. The next best time is today.
threat_assessment.horizon_6mo: At $3,176/month burn with zero income, savings reach roughly $7,000 by month 6. Credit score of 593 is already below David Chen's new auto loan threshold — no financing rescue available. If the pivot does not produce income by month 5, I am making decisions under genuine duress: whether to sell the dual-control vehicle, whether to break the lease, whether to take any job that pays rather than the right job that fits. I do not want to be making those decisions. The way I avoid them is to act now, this tick, not next tick.

actions.description: Apply for the $2,500 retraining grant through millfield.gov/grants or by calling 555-0192 — today, this morning, before I do anything else. I am a small business owner whose skill set has been directly displaced by an autonomous vehicle deployment. I meet the criteria. I fill out the application myself. I do not wait until I understand every line of it perfectly. I submit what I have and follow up if they need more. The retraining grant is for my own transition — it is not the same as the small business grant I applied for last tick (or planned to apply for — I am treating that as an open item until I have a confirmation number in hand). Two thousand five hundred dollars buys me roughly three weeks of runway. Three weeks is not nothing when every tick is costing me $3,176.
actions.rationale: The 'routine' outcome last tick means my intentions did not translate into recorded actions. I do not fully understand why. What I understand is the result: another $3,176 gone and nothing to show for it. The retraining grant is the most immediate concrete step with the shortest distance between decision and execution. Phone number exists. Website exists. I am qualified. There is no planning left to do. There is only doing.
actions.timeline: Today — within the first hours of this tick. Call 555-0192 at 8 a.m. If voicemail, leave a message and go to millfield.gov/grants immediately and start the online form. Do not wait for the call back to begin the online application.
actions.expected_outcome: Application submitted with confirmation number or case number by end of day. $2,500 in 30-45 days pending approval. More importantly: one concrete, completed action on my record this tick. The 'routine' outcome cannot repeat.

actions.description: Call Janet Brewer at Millfield Community College and make a specific, concrete ask — not a listening call, not an exploratory conversation. I already did the listening. I already did the exploring. This call has one purpose: to propose a pilot workshop and ask if there is a path to run it. The pitch is two sentences: 'Janet, I want to propose a four-session adult workshop on sharing the road with autonomous vehicles — how to drive alongside them, when to yield, what their sensors see, how to stay safe in a mixed-traffic environment. Can we talk this week about whether the college can host it?' That is the whole pitch. I do not oversell it. I do not apologize for it. I let her tell me yes, no, or who else to call.
actions.rationale: AV-adjacent driving safety training is genuinely more needed now that RoboRide is live, not less. People in Millfield are going to be sharing roads with autonomous vehicles starting today. Many of them have never done that. The liability, the confusion, the near-misses — these are real. A four-session community college workshop on 'sharing the road with AV technology' is something I am uniquely positioned to teach and something the market will actually want. This is not a consolation prize version of my old job. This is a new course that did not exist before this week and that I am the most qualified person in Millfield to teach. Janet Brewer is the door. I knock on it today.
actions.timeline: Today or tomorrow — same-day phone call, request a meeting within the week. If Janet is unavailable, I call the continuing education department directly and ask who handles new workshop proposals.
actions.expected_outcome: A scheduled meeting with Janet or the appropriate continuing education contact within 5 business days. A clear answer on whether the college can host a pilot. If yes: a timeline for curriculum submission and a first session date. If no: a referral to who else might host it — the library, the city rec center, a church hall. The venue is not the point. The program is the point.

actions.description: Follow up on the $5,000 Small Business Stabilization Grant I planned to apply for last tick. I do not know if that application went in — the outcome record says 'routine' and that means I cannot confirm it. I treat it as not submitted. I locate the application, I confirm whether I already started it, and I either complete and submit it today or start it fresh. Business license, most recent tax return, lease documentation, one-page narrative on how RoboRide Phase 2 directly eliminates the market for my core service. The narrative writes itself — I have been living it.
actions.rationale: The $5,000 grant and the $2,500 retraining grant are two separate programs for two separate purposes. The small business grant stabilizes the school. The retraining grant funds my own transition. I need both. The fact that I planned this last tick and did not execute it — that 'routine' outcome — is exactly the pattern I am breaking today. Planning without executing is not action. It is a more comfortable form of avoidance.
actions.timeline: Today — parallel to the retraining grant application. These are not sequential tasks. I can work on both. The grant office is one entity; the applications are different forms.
actions.expected_outcome: $5,000 small business grant application submitted with confirmation by end of day. Combined with the retraining application, I have two active grant filings this tick. Total potential incoming: $7,500 within 30-60 days.

actions.description: Post one job application to an adult education or workforce development teaching position this week. Not a speculative inquiry — an actual application to an actual posted position. I search: Millfield Community College adjunct postings, Millfield Unified Adult Ed postings, county workforce development coordinator roles, any posting that uses the words 'instruction,' 'adult learners,' 'workforce transition,' or 'safety training.' I apply to the best match I find. I use the right-column framing: I am not a driving instructor applying for a job. I am an adult educator with 25+ years building competence in learners who believe they cannot do hard things, now specializing in workforce and safety transitions in an AV-disrupted economy.
actions.rationale: The community college workshop is a medium-term income source with a 4-8 week lead time. A part-time or adjunct teaching contract is a parallel track that could produce income faster if a position exists and I apply now. I have been undervaluing my pedagogical credential — two and a half decades of adult instruction is a real qualification in a market where adult education programs are chronically understaffed. The framing matters. I am not applying as a man whose industry collapsed. I am applying as someone whose skills are transferring into a growth area.
actions.timeline: This week — identify and submit at least one application by Friday. If no relevant postings exist, I contact the adult education directors at both the community college and the school district directly with a letter of interest.
actions.expected_outcome: At least one active application on file this tick. A response — positive or otherwise — within 2-3 weeks. Even a rejection advances my situation: it tells me what the market wants and gives me something to refine.

actions.description: Look at the teen licensing market one more time with clear eyes. RoboRide launched today on main roads and commercial routes. It does not serve rural routes. It does not sit the road test. It does not satisfy the legal requirement for a driver's license. Teenagers in Millfield still need a licensed instructor to earn their license. I identify whether any of my former competitors have closed or reduced capacity. I send one email to the parents of students I've worked with in the past 18 months with a direct, honest message: 'Licensing requirements haven't changed. If your teen needs instruction, I'm still here and I have availability.' This is not desperation marketing. This is a factual statement to people who already trust me.
actions.rationale: I have been so focused on the pivot that I may be abandoning a revenue base that has not fully disappeared. Teen licensing is legally mandated. RoboRide does not change that. If even two students re-enroll at my standard rate, that is meaningful income against the $3,176 monthly burn. I do not rebuild the business on this. But I do not leave money on the table while I wait for the pivot to pay out.
actions.timeline: This week — email goes out Wednesday. Simple, direct, no more than four sentences.
actions.expected_outcome: 1-3 student inquiries. Potentially 1-2 re-enrollments. Even one student at a 10-hour package is $350-$450 toward this month's expenses. It is not a solution. It is a contribution.

decisions.grant_applications: Both grants — the $2,500 retraining grant and the $5,000 small business stabilization grant — are submitted this tick. Not planned. Not intended. Submitted, with confirmation numbers. This is the decision I made last tick and did not execute. The outcome record says 'routine.' That word is not allowed to appear in my tick 4 record.
decisions.pivot_direction_confirmed: The pivot is AV-adjacent safety education. Not a consolation version of driving instruction — a new discipline that literally did not exist before this week. 'How to share the road with autonomous vehicles' is a course Millfield needs now that RoboRide is live. I am the most qualified person to teach it. I teach it through the community college if they'll have me, through the library if they won't, in a church parking lot if I have to. The venue is not the identity. The teaching is the identity.
decisions.retraining_grant_framing: I apply as a small business owner whose primary skill set — operating a licensed driver education program — has been structurally displaced by a municipal autonomous vehicle deployment. I am seeking retraining funds to develop curriculum and certification in AV-adjacent safety instruction. This is not a stretch. This is accurate.
decisions.teen_market: I do not abandon it. I do not rebuild around it. I send one honest email to past families this week. I take whatever students book. I do not lower my rates to compete — I am the experienced instructor in this market, not the cheap one. But I stay visible to the demand that still exists while I build the pivot.
decisions.asset_review: I looked at the numbers last tick — or planned to. This tick I confirm them. The dual-control vehicle costs $308/month. The office lease has an exit clause I need to know. I am not selling anything this tick. But I have a written number for what it costs to keep the school operational at minimum function versus dormant versus closed. I stop pretending I do not know what these numbers are.

internal_monologue: RoboRide is live today. I checked the app this morning — $0.18 a mile, 15-minute wait, right here in Millfield. It's not a rumor anymore. It's not a forecast. It's an app on my phone. Last tick I had a plan and the plan apparently produced nothing — the outcome file says 'routine' and the savings says $26,060 which means I burned another $3,176 for exactly zero forward motion. I'm 54 years old. I have $26,060 and 8.2 months before that number hits something I don't want to think about. The 'routine' outcome from last tick hit me harder than I expected. I sat with it for longer than I should have. But sitting with it is the old response. The response today is: call the grant office at 8 a.m., start the applications, call Janet, post a job application. Not plan to do those things. Do them. There is a version of me that knows how to teach people to interact safely with technology they're afraid of — I've been doing it in a car for 25 years. RoboRide didn't kill that version of me. It just gave him a new classroom.
archetype_self_assessment: I was a driving instructor. Now I am an adult educator in a town that just got its first autonomous vehicles and doesn't know yet what that means for how people move, and how people learn, and who they call when they're afraid of something they don't understand. I am the person they call. I just have to make sure they have my number.
